cards.text: It's the fifth month of the fourth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, and the prophet Jeremiah has a yoke on his neck. Another prophet comes up to him: Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon. And friend, Hananiah does NOT pull him aside for a quiet little chat.

cards.question: Where does Hananiah say his piece to Jeremiah, with the priests and all the people watching?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

cards.question: Hananiah says the LORD of Hosts has a message, and it goes like this: I have broken the ___ of the king of Babylon.
Hananiah says the articles that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, carried off from the house of the LORD will be brought back. How soon?
Hananiah also says the LORD will bring back Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah who was carried off to Babylon, along with all the exiles from Judah. True or false?

cards.text: Now it's Jeremiah's turn to answer, yoke on his neck, with the priests and all the people standing right there. No pressure, Jeremiah!

cards.question: Jeremiah's first word back to Hananiah is "Amen!" True or false?

cards.text: And he means it: may the LORD bring the articles and the exiles back from Babylon. Then he says "Nevertheless," and friend, that's the prophet version of "I LOVE your cookies, BUT."
Jeremiah says the prophets of old, the ones who came before him and Hananiah, prophesied war, disaster and plague against many lands and great kingdoms.

cards.question: Jeremiah says a prophet who prophesies peace will be recognized as truly sent by the LORD only if his word comes ___.

cards.text: Hananiah's next move isn't a speech. He takes the yoke right off Jeremiah's neck.

cards.question: Hananiah has the yoke from Jeremiah's neck in his hands. What does he do with it?

answers.text: He throws it in the fire

cards.question: Then Hananiah tells all the people that in this way, within two years, the LORD will break Nebuchadnezzar's yoke off the neck of all the ___.
Right after Hananiah breaks the yoke, Jeremiah fires back at him with a new word from the LORD on the spot. True or false?

cards.text: Jeremiah just goes on his way, and friend, if somebody snapped MY handle in front of a crowd, you'd hear me yelling from the Dorinverse. But shortly after, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah.

cards.question: The LORD sends Jeremiah back with a message for Hananiah: Hananiah broke a yoke of wood. What does the LORD say Hananiah has made in its place?

cards.text: The LORD says He has put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations to make them serve Nebuchadnezzar, and they WILL serve him. He's even given him control of the beasts of the field.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells Hananiah: Listen, Hananiah! The LORD did not send you, but you have persuaded this people to trust in a ___.
Then Jeremiah gives Hananiah the LORD's word: the LORD is about to remove him from the face of the earth. When does the LORD say Hananiah will die?

cards.text: The LORD says it's because Hananiah has preached rebellion against the LORD. Hananiah promised two years, and in the seventh month of that very year, the prophet Hananiah died.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-thought ("In the fifth month of that same year"), and the yoke is the center of the whole passage. Card 1 says Jeremiah has a yoke on his neck but never says why. In Jer 27:2, 12, the LORD told him to wear it as a sign that the nations must serve the king of Babylon. Without that context, the baker can't follow what Hananiah breaking it means, or why the LORD answers with a yoke of iron.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Card 1 states that Jeremiah has a yoke on his neck, but it cites only Jeremiah 28:1, which says nothing about a yoke. That detail comes from Jer 27:2 (or 28:10) and needs its reference.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 6 says Jeremiah answers "yoke on his neck" but cites only Jeremiah 28:5, which doesn't mention the yoke. The yoke detail comes from outside 28:5 (Jer 27:2 or 28:10).

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "No pressure, Jeremiah!" is a stock line that reads as mildly pleasant, not laugh-out-loud. This is a big public moment, a prophet answering another prophet in front of the priests and all the people, and it can hold a real laugh.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. ... If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: "And he means it" states Jeremiah's sincerity as fact. The text gives only his words ("Amen! May the LORD do so!") and never says what he felt. Any guess at his sincerity must be marked as Papa Dorin's own.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question: what kind of yoke has Hananiah made? The wrong answers, "A yoke of straw" and "A yoke of rope," are invented. They are not real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
